name: REF02CSZ-REEL7
title: REF01/REF02/REF03: 10.0 V, 5.0 V and 2.5 V precision band gap voltage references
summary: Three series voltage references with fixed outputs of 10.0 V (REF01), 5.0 V (REF02) and 2.5 V (REF03), running from up to 36 V and sourcing up to 10 mA. A TRIM pin adjusts the output by a few percent, and a TEMP pin brings out a band gap voltage that rises about 1.96 mV/°C. Grades differ in initial accuracy and drift. REF02CSZ-REEL7 is the 5.0 V C-grade part (±50 mV, 65 ppm/°C max) in 8-lead SOIC on tape and reel, rated −40 °C to +85 °C.
key_figures: up to 36 V; REF02 7.0 V to 36 V
10 mA source (8 mA C grade), 0.3 mA sink

circuits.title: Input and output capacitors
circuits.description: The reference with a 0.1 µF capacitor from the input to ground and another from the output to ground. TEMP and TRIM are left open.

circuits.title: Optional trim adjustment
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ potentiometer sits between the output and a 1 kΩ resistor to ground; its wiper drives TRIM through 470 kΩ. Turning the pot moves the output a few percent either side of nominal (adjustment range table). Low-tempco resistors keep the reference's own drift unchanged.

circuits.title: Temperature monitoring
circuits.description: An AD8641 wired as a unity-gain follower buffers the TEMP pin, so the reference output is disturbed by less than 100 µV. The buffered voltage tracks die temperature at about 1.9 mV/°C. The op amp runs from 15 V; TRIM is left open.

circuits.title: Burn-in circuit
circuits.description: The part runs between +18 V and −18 V rails for burn-in: VIN is fed from +18 V through 10 Ω, GND sits on −18 V, and each rail has a 10 µF capacitor to ground. A resistive load from VOUT to ground is optional; load current stays at or below 10 mA.

circuits.title: Basic reference application
circuits.description: The plain hookup for any of the three voltages: 0.1 µF from input to ground and 0.1 µF from output to ground. Other values work if they keep to the input and output capacitor guidance.

circuits.title: Simple current source
circuits.description: The reference floats on its load: RSET runs from VOUT to the node VL, the GND pin also returns to VL, and RL goes from VL to ground. The load carries ISET = (VOUT − VL)/RSET plus the quiescent current IQ (about 0.6 mA). IQ varies from about 0.55 mA to 0.65 mA, which limits this to low-precision use.

circuits.title: Programmable 0 mA to 5 mA current source
circuits.description: An OP1177 drives the REF02 ground pin so that the voltage between the AD5201 wiper and B end, set by the digital code, appears across RSET (1 kΩ). The load current is VREF × D / RSET. The REF02 ground moves between −5 V and VL as the pot sweeps, so the op amp runs from split supplies, ±12 V in this circuit.

parts.note: digital potentiometer; digital pins not drawn

notes: VOUT swings 0 V to (5 V + VL); the REF02 ground swings −5 V to VL.

circuits.title: Precision boosted output regulator
circuits.description: An OP1177 compares the output VO with the reference voltage and drives the gate of a 2N7002 through 100 Ω, so the MOSFET passes load current straight from VIN. Feedback returns from VO through 100 Ω to the inverting input, with 1000 pF from the op amp output to that input. With these parts it supplies up to 50 mA from 15 V; a larger MOSFET raises that.

circuits.title: Bipolar voltage reference
circuits.description: A REF03 gives +2.5 V, and an OP97 inverting amplifier with two 100 kΩ resistors (gain −1) makes −2.5 V from it. A low-offset op amp keeps the negative output accurate.
notes: Pin numbers: REF03 VIN 2, VOUT 6, GND 4; OP97 −IN 2, +IN 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V− 4.

circuits.title: Negatively adjustable reference
circuits.description: A 50 kΩ potentiometer across the REF03 output feeds the non-inverting input of an OP97; the inverting input takes the REF03 output through 50 kΩ, with 50 kΩ feedback. The output runs from +2.5 V with the wiper at the top to −2.5 V with it at the bottom. The op amp supplies the load, so it needs low offset and enough output current.
notes: Pin numbers: REF03 VIN 2, VOUT 6, GND 4; OP97 −IN 2, +IN 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V− 4.

operation.text: REF01, REF02 and REF03 are series references giving 10.0 V, 5.0 V and 2.5 V. They come in 8-lead SOIC, PDIP, CERDIP and TO-99, and in a 20-terminal LCC for 883 parts. All three share one pinout. The ADR01, ADR02, ADR03 and ADR06 are named as the parts for new designs, with better accuracy and drift over a wider temperature range and the same pins. These figures cover commercial grades; 883 parts have their own data.

Inside is a band gap cell of two NPN transistors whose emitter areas differ by two to one. Their VBE difference sets a current proportional to absolute temperature; added to one VBE, it gives a band gap voltage that is nearly flat with temperature. An internal amplifier with a resistor divider scales this up to 10.0 V, 5.0 V or 2.5 V. Laser trimming of resistors sets initial accuracy, curvature and drift.

The part is stable with no external capacitors. A 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor from VOUT to ground is the recommended addition: it improves stability and filters low-level noise. Adding 1 µF to 10 µF (ceramic, tantalum or electrolytic) in parallel with it improves the response to fast load-current steps, at the cost of a longer turn-on time. On VIN, 1 µF to 10 µF of the same types improves the response where the supply moves, and 0.1 µF ceramic beside it reduces supply noise. All of these capacitors sit as close to the pins as possible.

TRIM moves the output above or below its factory value, to take out system errors such as line and load shifts, thermal hysteresis or offset after solder reflow. The basic network is a 10 kΩ pot from VOUT to a 1 kΩ resistor to ground, its wiper into TRIM through 470 kΩ; the reachable range for each model is in the adjustment range table. With low-tempco resistors in this network, the reference's temperature performance changes little.

The TEMP pin carries a voltage taken straight from the band gap core, linear in temperature: about 550 mV at 25 °C, rising about 1.96 mV/°C. It is a convenience rather than a precision feature. Because it is unbuffered, any current into or out of TEMP shifts VOUT; a few tens of microamps can push the output out of regulation. A low-bias op amp buffer (AD8601 or AD8641) keeps the shift in VOUT under 100 µV.

Typical drift seen in development is about 50 ppm after 1000 hours of continuous unloaded running at 25 °C, for every output voltage. Long-term stability is not guaranteed; the output can shift past 50 ppm at any time, most of all in the first 200 hours. Application note AN-713 covers long-term drift.
Running the part powered for a long period before use reduces later long-term drift. A resistive load during burn-in is optional; keep its current at or below 10 mA.

Up to 10 mA can be sourced at room temperature over the whole input range. At high ambient temperatures input voltage and load current must keep dissipation within the package rating (power dissipation equation); operating beyond it risks early failure or damage.
Quiescent current stays nearly constant as load current changes, which allows the reference to serve as a simple current source.

Line regulation is the output change for a given input change, given in %/V, ppm/V or µV/V. Load regulation is the output change for a given load current change, in µV/mA, ppm/mA or ohms of output resistance. Both include self-heating.
